title: NFL Strength of Schedule: Dallas Cowboys Facing Tough 2026 Season - NewsBreak
text:
By Angelo Guinhawa ,
40 minutes ago The Dallas Cowboys are entering the 2026 NFL season with a demanding road ahead. Early projections have placed their schedule among the toughest in the league, setting the stage for a challenging campaign.
Dallas faces one of the more difficult strength of schedules based on projected opponent performance. Their slate ranks near the upper tier in difficulty, reflecting a lineup filled with teams expected to contend at a high level.
Dec 21, 2025; Arlington, Texas, USA; Dallas Cowboys quarterback Dak Prescott (4) celebrates with wide receiver George Pickens (3) following a touchdown pass caught by Pickens during the second quarter at AT&T Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Kevin Jairaj-Imagn Images A significant portion of that challenge comes from the depth of competition rather than just a few marquee matchups. Week after week, the Cowboys are set to face opponents capable of testing both sides of the ball, leaving little room for extended stretches of recovery.
The NFC East remains a factor as well, with divisional games continuing to carry intensity and unpredictability. Combined with strong non-division opponents, the overall structure of the schedule creates a consistent level of pressure throughout the season.
Dallas Cowboys’ Strength of Schedule for 2026 NFL Season Among the Hardest Nov 3, 2025; Arlington, Texas, USA; Quarterback Dak Prescott (4) warms up before the game against the Arizona Cardinals at AT&T Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Kevin Jairaj-Imagn Images Dallas’ strength of schedule is among the hardest in the league ahead of next season. This can be seen in an update shared by Warren Sharp for the Sharp Analysis.

29 Dallas Cowboys 8.5 For Dallas, the demanding schedule arrives at a time when the team is aiming to reestablish itself as a contender. Navigating such a difficult path will require discipline, depth and the ability to perform under sustained pressure.
The challenge, however, also presents an opportunity to prove resilience. If the Cowboys can meet the demands of their schedule, they could position themselves as a stronger and more battle-tested team by the end of the 2026 season.
